name: Ferdinand Lauren
headline: I turn observations into systems people can rely on.
positioning: Entry-level IT business analyst and ERP functional consultant. Computer Science undergraduate at Universitas Lampung, working on the layer before software: reading how an operation runs, writing what the system must do, and proving the result.
availability: Open to internship, trainee programme and junior positions in ERP, enterprise systems and digital transformation.

process.label: Observe
process.note: Read the operation as it actually runs, not as the SOP says it runs.
detail: Watch where work changes hands, and where it waits.
Separate what I saw from what I only suspect.
Write every friction with the evidence beside it.

process.label: Define
process.note: Turn friction into a problem statement and a scope boundary.
detail: Name the actors and the handoffs between them.
Decide what is in scope, what is out, and why.
Give each requirement an ID so it can be traced.

process.label: Design
process.note: Translate requirements into behaviour before thinking about screens.
detail: Model the things that change as explicit states.
Describe data by what it means to the business.
Specify failure codes and the manual fallback.
process.artifact: State machines · data model · error catalogue

process.label: Verify
process.note: Write the expected behaviour first, then check it and record what is still unknown.
detail: Turn each rule into a numbered acceptance scenario.
Automate what can be automated; report the rest honestly.
Mark every claim that no evidence supports.

approachCaveat: This is my working approach, practised on one independent concept project and on coursework. It is not a methodology validated in client engagements.
